summary: Attacked the link map for the Tau Ceti roadmap 'Root systems, Weyl groups, and the Cartan-Killing classification': 19 outgoing links, 7 overlaps, 217 roadmaps examined. No finding. Every one of the 38 evidence records quotes its source verbatim and at the exact line range it cites; the screening covers every roadmap in the atlas; an independent sweep by root-system vocabulary, and a second by the subtler topics that depend on root systems without naming them, turned up no roadmap that should have been linked and was not; and every document in the atlas that cites RootSystems by name or path is linked. The map's own structural claims — no stage edge incident to RootSystems, and the links it deliberately omits because another packet records them — check out.
checked: Coverage against the atlas. The map's `examined` array holds 217 roadmap records and its links reach 7 more; the atlas index currently lists 211 roadmaps, and every one of them is either examined or linked, with nothing left unscreened. Seven examined ids are no longer in the index (AnalyticHabiroStack, AnalyticStacks, FoundationsAndLibraryIntegration, MordellLawrenceVenkatesh, QWittVectors, RingStacksAndTransmutation, SolidAnalyticRings), which is drift since the recorded snapshot — the map states 212 roadmaps in the atlas at the revision it read — and means it screened more than exists now, not less.

Every evidence record on both sides of every link: 38 in all, each carrying a sourcePath, a quote and a startLine/endLine. Every quote appears verbatim in its cited file, and every one appears within the exact line range cited, with no off-by-one tolerance needed. Zero failures on either test.

Whether an `explicit` confidence is earned. Of the 11 explicit links, 10 have an evidence quote that names the other roadmap or a declaration shared by both sides — `DynkinType.IsLongSimpleRoot` for the CFSG index glue, `DynkinType.simplyConnectedRootDatum` (whose consumer quote even reads '(root systems Layer 6)') for the ambient-group carrier, `DynkinType.cartanMatrix` for the graph-twisted Steinberg maps. The eleventh, the chamber link to ClassicalGroups, is the one whose two quotes state the same mathematics — the dominant cone as `0 <= P.coroot' i x` on one side and the weakly decreasing `DominantWeight n` on the other — without sharing a name. Not reported: both texts state the dependency, and the link's own reason says it 'supplies the cone definition and its real root-space geometry only' and warns the consumer not to apply a real ordered-field theorem directly.

Links the map might have missed, by an independent sweep rather than by trusting its screening. Every stage of every roadmap in the atlas was searched for root-system vocabulary (root system, root datum, RootPairing, RootDatum, Weyl group, Dynkin, Cartan matrix, Cartan-Killing, simple roots, positive roots, coroot, Coxeter). Every roadmap with three or more mentions is linked or overlapped — CFSGStatement, QuiverRepresentations, LieHighestWeight, LieGroups, ReductiveGroups, ClassicalGroups, GrothendieckEulerForms, IntegralLattices — with the single exception of ZigzagPreprojective, and that is deliberate and documented: its examined record says the matching link and overlap 'are already recorded in the live Zigzag packet and are omitted here to avoid duplication', and `alreadyRecorded` carries that packet with one link and one overlap stage.

A second sweep for the topics that depend on root systems without using the vocabulary: ADE classifications, du Val and simple singularities, del Pezzo lattices, Iwahori-Hecke algebras, crystal bases, Kac-Moody and affine root systems, Tits buildings, nilpotent orbits and Springer theory, Bruhat decompositions, Macdonald polynomials and flag varieties. Du Val singularities, del Pezzo surfaces, crystal bases, nilpotent orbits and Macdonald polynomials appear nowhere in the atlas. The Hecke-algebra, Bruhat and flag-variety hits are automorphic and Shimura roadmaps using them as established tools rather than as root-system consumers. The one real candidate raised was ReductiveGroupsPartII, whose RG2.1 builds affine root systems and RG2.2 buildings.

That candidate, in the source rather than by title. The map's examined note reads 'RG2.1 explicitly keeps absolute roots with ReductiveGroups and includes multipliable relative roots; buildings, parahorics and integral duality remain PartII, not RootSystems.' RG2.1's text ends with the sentence 'Absolute roots remain supplied by ReductiveGroups', so the note is exact. RG2.5's 'pinned split dual group over Z from the dual root datum' is not a missed link either: RootSystems takes root-datum duality from Mathlib, its Layer 6 saying 'The adjoint form is `RootPairing.flip` of the dual type's datum, not a second pinned definition', so the dual datum reaches RG2.5 through ReductiveGroups and the library rather than from this roadmap.

The sharpest objective test of omission: which documents in the atlas cite RootSystems by name or by document path at all. Exactly three do — CFSGStatement, ReductiveGroups and SpinRepresentations — and all three are linked. Nothing cites this roadmap without being connected to it.

The map's structural claim about the input graph, that there is 'no recorded stage edge incident to RootSystems at the audited snapshot'. Still true of the current atlas: counting both `stageEdges` records and stage `requires` entries across every roadmap extract gives zero edges incident to any RootSystems stage, so the map is not silently contradicted by edges recorded since.

The seven overlaps, read in full. Each names the stages on both sides, gives a detail and recommends rescope or keep, and each is a real observation rather than a restatement of a link. Two are worth recording as work the map did rather than missed: overlap 2 finds that ClassicalGroups names a GL_n root datum from RootSystems although GL_n's central-character lattice is outside RootSystems' stated scope, and overlap 4 finds a hypothesis mismatch — the consumer allows nonreduced restricted root systems while the supplier assumes reducedness — and declines to assert an unconditional chamber edge on that basis.
